text:
alex: Heads up — running into an annoying CORS + cookie SameSite issue on RN WebView when trying to stream server events for mobile chat. Works in Chrome but Safari-based WebViews drop the cookie on redirect. Anyone seen this? (RN 0.71)

maria: Hmm — are you using cookies for auth or Authorization header? Safari has aggressive ITP + SameSite enforcement. If you rely on cookies you need SameSite=None; Secure AND the server must allow credentials.

sam: For streaming (SSE / chunked responses) I usually prefer bearer header. WebView fetch with credentials: 'include' is flaky across iOS. Headers approach avoids SameSite pitfalls and matches our SDK behavior.

alex: Right now server is issuing a short-lived cookie via redirect from /auth -> /chat. Example: `Set-Cookie: sid=...; SameSite=None; Secure; Max-Age=300`. The WebView seems to ignore it on the redirect chain.

julie: For RN specifically, if you can, pass the ephemeral token into the WebView via injected JS or `postMessage` from native side, then set `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on the client fetch that opens the SSE. That avoids relying on cookie mechanics in the WebView.

sam: +1. Also ensure your server CORS allows `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` and `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization,Content-Type`. Example preflight: `res.set('Access-Control-Allow-Credentials','true')`.

alex: Thanks — I can change to header flow. Quick question on streaming reconnects: if SSE dies we want exponential backoff but preserve the same session token. Any recommended retry logic?

maria: Keep retries on client with jitter, starting ~300ms doubling to ~8s, and if you hit max attempts, call native to refresh token. Avoid reauth too often. Also keep a small buffer of last event id and pass `Last-Event-ID` header to resume when possible.

julie: For people hitting this later: code we use in RN WebView (pseudo):
```
const ev = new EventSource(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
ev.onopen = () => { /* reset backoff */ }
ev.onerror = () => { /* backoff + reconnect */ }
```
Note: some WebView versions don't support EventSource with headers — in that case use fetch + ReadableStream chunk parsing.

alex: I pushed a tiny SDK change to prefer Authorization header for webview flows and added a reconnect helper. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/1234 PTAL @maria @sam :eyes:

maria: Reviewing now. One nit: please add a fallback to `fetch`-based streaming when `EventSource` fails (user-agent feature detect).

sam: Also add a small unit test that simulates a 401 during reconnect and checks the SDK triggers `onAuthExpired` so host app can refresh token.

dev-bot: CI passed — build 4128 on main. :white_check_mark:

alex: Great — thanks all. I'll update the PR with fetch fallback + test and merge after review. Leaving a note in the mobile SDK checklist about "avoid cookies in WebView".

maria: Thanks — this should reduce a bunch of flaky Safari bugs.
